story.head: DeBrincat’s favorite opponent
paras: The Red Wings (9-12-3) beat Vancouver 5-1 on Wednesday, while the Blue Jackets (9-13-1) lost 3-2 in a shootout to New Jersey the same night. Going in, the Red Wings are seventh in the Atlantic (tied for 26th in the NHL) and the Blue Jackets seventh in the Metropolitan (29th).

The Red Wings have played better than their record (.438) says: their chances are worth about .535, and their finishing has held them back. So have the Blue Jackets (.413 on chances worth .500), where their finishing has held them back.

The Red Wings block more shots than almost anyone (3rd), but ice the puck a lot (29th). The Blue Jackets lean on their stars as much as almost anyone (2nd most) and do a lot of their shooting from distance (2nd most). Columbus has scored 2.43 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Red Wings’ power play (5th) could do real damage against the Blue Jackets’ penalty kill (23rd). Beyond that, the Blue Jackets’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Wings’ not so much.

Lucas Raymond (10 G / 13 A / 23 P in 24 GP) leads the Red Wings in scoring, and Viktor Arvidsson (9 G / 9 A / 18 P in 24 GP) is next in line. For the Blue Jackets, Kent Johnson (9 G / 14 A / 23 P in 23 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Zach Werenski (5 G / 16 A / 21 P in 23 GP) is next in line.
John Gibson (4-8-1 / .862 SV% in 14 GS) has struggled for Detroit so far, but is expected to start. Jet Greaves (2-8-0 / .875 SV% in 10 GS) is expected to go for Columbus.
